Q 41:49–50 · Vol. 4, pp. 204–205

Verses 49 to 50

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Man does not tire of supplication for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless (49) And if We let him taste mercy from Us after hardship has touched him, he will surely say: This is due to me; and I do not think the Hour will occur; and if I am returned to my Lord, indeed for me with Him is the best. But We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste of a harsh punishment (50)
لا يَسْأَمُ الْإِنْسانُ مِنْ دُعاءِ الْخَيْرِ وَإِنْ مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَيَؤُسٌ قَنُوطٌ (49) وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ هذا لِي وَما أَظُنُّ السَّاعَةَ قائِمَةً وَلَئِنْ رُجِعْتُ إِلى رَبِّي إِنَّ لِي عِنْدَهُ لَلْحُسْنى فَلَنُنَبِّئَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِما عَمِلُوا وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ غَلِيظٍ (50)
Vol. 4, p. 205
"From supplication for good": from seeking abundance in wealth and blessing. Ibn Mas'ud read: "min du'a'in bil-khayr." "And if evil touches him": that is, hardship and poverty, "he is despairing and hopeless": exaggeration is used in it from two directions: from the direction of the pattern fa'ul, and from the direction of repetition. And "qunut" is that the trace of despair appears on him, so that he shrinks and is broken; that is, he cuts off hope from the bounty of God and His relief; and this is the attribute of the disbeliever, by the proof of His saying, Exalted, "Indeed, none despairs of the relief of God except the disbelieving people." And when We relieve him with health after illness, or ease after hardship, he says "This is mine" (li), that is: this is my right that has reached me, because I deserved it through the good, merit, and works of righteousness I have; or: this is mine and will not leave me. Like it is His saying, Exalted, "But when good came to them, they said: This is ours"; and like it His saying, Exalted, "And I do not think the Hour will occur ... We only assume it a conjecture, and we are not convinced" — he means: and I do not think it will come to be; and if it should be, by way of supposition, "indeed for me with God is the best" condition, of honor and blessing [as printed], comparing the affair of the Hereafter to the affair of this world. And from one of them: the disbeliever has two wishes: he says in this world, "and if I am returned to my Lord, indeed for me with Him is the best," and he says in the Hereafter, "Would that I were dust." It is also said: it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. "We will surely inform them" of the reality of what they did of deeds that necessitate punishment. "And We will surely make them see" the reverse of what they believed concerning them, namely that they deserve honor and nearness with God because of them: "And We shall turn to whatever deed they did and make it as dust scattered." And that is because they used to spend their wealth for show before people and for seeking boasting and arrogance, nothing more, and they used to reckon that what they were upon was a cause of wealth and health, and that they were entitled to that.
مِنْ دُعاءِ الْخَيْرِ من طلب السعة في المال والنعمة. وقرأ ابن مسعود: من دعاء بالخير وَإِنْ مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ أى الضيقة والفقر فَيَؤُسٌ قَنُوطٌ بولغ فيه من طريقين: من طريق بناء فعول، ومن طريق التكرير والقنوط أن يظهر عليه أثر اليأس فيتضاءل وينكسر، أى: يقطع الرجاء من فضل الله وروحه، وهذه صفة الكافر بدليل قوله تعالى إِنَّهُ لا يَيْأَسُ مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْكافِرُونَ وإذا فرجنا عنه بصحة بعد مرض أو سعة بعد ضيق قال هذا لِي أى هذا حقي وصل إلىّ، لأنى استوجبته بما عندي من خير وفضل وأعمال برّ. أو هذا لي لا يزول عنى، ونحوه قوله تعالى فَإِذا جاءَتْهُمُ الْحَسَنَةُ قالُوا لَنا هذِهِ ونحوه قوله تعالى وَما أَظُنُّ السَّاعَةَ قائِمَةً إِنْ نَظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنًّا وَما نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ يريد: وما أظنها تكون، فإن كانت على طريق التوهم إِنَّ لِي عند الله الحالة الحسنى من للكرامة والنعمة، قائسا أمر الاخرة على أمر الدنيا. وعن بعضهم: للكافر أمنيتان، يقول في الدنيا: ولئن رجعت إلى ربى إنّ لي عنده للحسنى. ويقول في الآخرة: يا ليتني كنت ترابا. وقيل: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة. فلنخبرنهم بحقيقة ما عملوا من الأعمال الموجبة للعذاب. ولنبصرنهم عكس ما اعتقدوا فيها أنهم يستوجبون عليها كرامة وقربة عند الله وَقَدِمْنا إِلى ما عَمِلُوا مِنْ عَمَلٍ فَجَعَلْناهُ هَباءً مَنْثُوراً وذلك أنهم كانوا ينفقون أموالهم رئاء الناس وطلبا للافتخار والاستكبار لا غير، وكانوا يحسبون أنّ ما هم عليه سبب الغنى والصحة، وأنهم محقوقون بذلك.

Vol. 4, p. 205
1. (1) . "Many a water I came to for the sake of Arwa, upon which the birds [gathered] like fallen leaves (lujayn); I startled the sandgrouse (qata) at it, and drove away from it the wolf's station, like the cursed man [scarecrow]." By al-Shammakh; and Arwa is the name of his beloved. And "al-lujayn" — with fatha on the lam and kasrah on the jim — is what falls of the leaf, from "al-lajn," which is pounding (al-daqq), because the wind or the shepherd strikes it, so it falls from the tree. And "dhara'tu" — with two fathas — means: I frightened the sandgrouse at it; and he singled it out because it is the quickest of the birds to water. And "the wolf's station" (maqam al-dhi'b) is his staying or the place of it, and he expressed by it a metonymy for his person; and he singled it out because the wolf's coming to water is mostly at night. And "the cursed man" (al-rajul al-la'in) is the figure set up in the middle of the crops in the shape of a man to drive away vermin. He says: many a water have I come to for the sake of my beloved, in the hope that she would come to it and I would see her. It is also narrated: "for union with Arwa," so perhaps it was an appointed meeting between them. And he likened the birds around the water to the leaves of the tree that fall, in dustiness, abundance, and scatter; and this shows that [the water] is not frequented much, so it is fit as a tryst for union. And "I startled ..." to the end is a metonymy for his coming at night; and "like the cursed man" is a circumstantial clause from the poet's pronoun, so it conveys that he preceded the sandgrouse and the wolf and sat there; or a circumstantial clause from the wolf, that is: in a frightening shape. And in it is proof of the poet's bravery and daring
1. (1) . وماء قد وردت لأجل أروى
…. عليه الطير كالورق اللجين ذعرت به القطا ونفيت عنه
…. مقام الذيب كالرجل اللعين للشماخ: وأروى، اسم محبوبته. واللجين- بفتح اللام وكسر الجيم-: ما يتساقط من الورق من اللجن وهو الدق، لأنه يضربه الهوى أو الراعي، فيسقط من الشجر. وذعرت- بفتحتين» أى: أخفت فيه القطا، وخصها لأنها أسبق الطير إلى الماء. ومقام الذيب: إقامته أو محلها، وعبر به كناية عن ذاته، وخصه لأن غالب وروده الماء ليلا. والرجل اللعين: هو الصورة التي تنصب وسط الزرع على شكل الرجل تطرد عنه الهوام، يقول: ورب ماء قد وردته لأجل محبوبتى، عسى أن تجيء عنده فأراها. ويروى: لوصل أروى، فلعله كان موعدا بينهما. وشبه الطير حول الماء بورق الشجر المتساقط في الكدرة والكثرة والانتشار، وهذا يدل على أنه لا يكثر وروده، فيصلح موعدا للوصل. وذعرت- إلى آخره: كناية عن وروده ليلا، وكالرجل اللعين: حال من ضمير الشاعر، فيفيد أنه سبق القطا والذيب وقعد هناك، أو حال من الذيب، أى: على هيئة مفزعة. وفيه دليل على شجاعة الشاعر وجرأته
29
Q 41:51 · Vol. 4, pp. 205–206

Verse 51

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, then he is full of lengthy supplication (51)
وَإِذا أَنْعَمْنا عَلَى الْإِنْسانِ أَعْرَضَ وَنَأى بِجانِبِهِ وَإِذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَذُو دُعاءٍ عَرِيضٍ (51)
Vol. 4, p. 205
This also is another kind of man's transgression: when God afflicts him with a blessing, the blessing makes him insolent, as though he had never met with hardship, so he forgets the Benefactor and turns away from thanking Him. "And distances himself with his side" means he went off with himself and became proud and magnified himself. And if harm and poverty touch him, he turns to constancy in supplication and sets about earnest entreaty and humble pleading. "Breadth" ('ard) has been metaphorically used for the abundance of supplication and its constancy, though it is an attribute of bodies; and length is also borrowed for it, just as thickness (ghilzah) is borrowed for severity of punishment. It is also read: "wa-na'a bijanibihi," with imalah of the alif and kasrah on the nun for assimilation; and "na'a" by metathesis, as they said "ra'a" for "ra'a" (to see).
هذا أيضا ضرب آخر من طغيان الإنسان إذا أصابه الله بنعمة أبطرته النعمة، وكأنه لم يلق بؤسا قط فنسي المنعم وأعرض عن شكره وَنَأى بِجانِبِهِ أى ذهب بنفسه وتكبر وتعظم. وإن مسه الضرّ والفقر: أقبل على دوام الدعاء وأخذ في الابتهال والتضرع. وقد استعير العرض لكثرة الدعاء ودوامه وهو من صفة الأجرام، ويستعار له الطول أيضا كما استعير الغلظ بشدّة العذاب. وقرئ: ونأى بجانبه، بإمالة الألف وكسر النون للإتباع. وناء على القلب، كما قالوا: راء في رأى.
Question
If you ask: make the meaning of His saying, Exalted, "wa-na'a bijanibihi" precise for me.
فإن قلت: حقق لي معنى قوله تعالى وَنَأى بِجانِبِهِ
Answer
I say: there are two aspects. One is that his "side" (janib) be put in the place of himself, as we mentioned regarding His saying, Exalted, "for what I neglected of the side (janb) of God," that the place of a thing and its direction are given the position of the thing itself; and from it comes the saying: "...... and I drove away from it ... the wolf's station ......" «1» ..
قلت: فيه وجهان: أن يوضع جانبه موضع نفسه كما ذكرنا في قوله تعالى عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ أن مكان الشيء وجهته ينزل منزلة الشيء نفسه، ومنه قوله: ......... ونفيت عنه … مقام الذئب...... «1» ..
Vol. 4, p. 206
he means: "and I drove the wolf away from it." And from it comes: "and for him who fears the station (maqam) of his Lord." And from it comes the saying of the scribes: "I attended so-and-so and his sitting-place (majlis)," and "I wrote to his side (jihah) and to his dear side (janib)," by which they mean his very self and person; so it is as though He had said: "and he distanced himself by himself (bi-nafsihi)," like their saying of the proud: "he went off with himself (dhahaba bi-nafsihi)," "conceit took him to every extreme," and "conceit blew about with him." And [the second aspect is] that what is meant by his "side" be his flank ('itf), and it would be an expression for deviation and turning aside, as they said: "he bent his flank (thana 'itfahu)," and "he turned away with his pillar (tawalla bi-ruknihi)."
يريد: ونفيت عنه الذئب. ومنه: ولمن خاف مقام ربه. ومنه قول الكتاب: حضرت فلان ومجلسه، وكتبت إلى جهته وإلى جانبه العزيز، يريدون نفسه وذاته، فكأنه قال: ونأى بنفسه، كقولهم في المتكبر: ذهب بنفسه، وذهبت به الخيلاء كل مذهب، وعصفت به الخيلاء، وأن يراد بجانبه: عطفه، ويكون عبارة عن الانحراف والازورار، كما قالوا: ثنى عطفه، وتولى بركنه.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 205
1. (1) . "Many a water I came to for the sake of Arwa, upon which the birds [gathered] like fallen leaves (lujayn); I startled the sandgrouse (qata) at it, and drove away from it the wolf's station, like the cursed man [scarecrow]." By al-Shammakh; and Arwa is the name of his beloved. And "al-lujayn" — with fatha on the lam and kasrah on the jim — is what falls of the leaf, from "al-lajn," which is pounding (al-daqq), because the wind or the shepherd strikes it, so it falls from the tree. And "dhara'tu" — with two fathas — means: I frightened the sandgrouse at it; and he singled it out because it is the quickest of the birds to water. And "the wolf's station" (maqam al-dhi'b) is his staying or the place of it, and he expressed by it a metonymy for his person; and he singled it out because the wolf's coming to water is mostly at night. And "the cursed man" (al-rajul al-la'in) is the figure set up in the middle of the crops in the shape of a man to drive away vermin. He says: many a water have I come to for the sake of my beloved, in the hope that she would come to it and I would see her. It is also narrated: "for union with Arwa," so perhaps it was an appointed meeting between them. And he likened the birds around the water to the leaves of the tree that fall, in dustiness, abundance, and scatter; and this shows that [the water] is not frequented much, so it is fit as a tryst for union. And "I startled ..." to the end is a metonymy for his coming at night; and "like the cursed man" is a circumstantial clause from the poet's pronoun, so it conveys that he preceded the sandgrouse and the wolf and sat there; or a circumstantial clause from the wolf, that is: in a frightening shape. And in it is proof of the poet's bravery and daring

Q 41:52 · Vol. 4, p. 206

Verse 52

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Say: Have you considered: if it is from God and then you disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition? (52)
قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ كَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ مَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ هُوَ فِي شِقاقٍ بَعِيدٍ (52)
Vol. 4, p. 206
"Have you considered" means "Tell me": "if the Qur'an is from God." He means that what you are upon, in denying the Qur'an and rejecting it, is not a matter issuing from a decisive proof by which you have attained certainty and the easing of hearts; rather it is, before examination and following the evidence, a possible matter: it may be from God, and it may not be from Him; and you have not examined and have not investigated; so what makes you deny that it could be true, when you have disbelieved in it? So tell me: who is more astray than you, when you have gone far in opposing it and being hostile to it, and perhaps it is true, so you have destroyed yourselves? And His saying, Exalted, "than one who is in extreme opposition" is put in the place of "than you," as a clarification of their condition and attribute.
أَرَأَيْتُمْ أخبرونى إِنْ كانَ القرآن مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ يعنى أن ما أنتم عليه من إنكار القرآن وتكذيبه ليس بأمر صادر عن حجة قاطعة حصلتم منها على اليقين وثلج الصدور، وإنما هو قبل النظر واتباع الدليل أمر محتمل، يجوز أن يكون من عند الله وأن لا يكون من عنده، وأنتم لم تنظروا ولم تفحصوا، فما أنكرتم أن يكون حقا وقد كفرتم به، فأخبرونى من أضلّ منكم وأنتم أبعدتم الشوط في مشاقته ومناصبته ولعله حق فأهلكتم أنفسكم؟ وقوله تعالى مِمَّنْ هُوَ فِي شِقاقٍ بَعِيدٍ موضوع موضع منكم، بيانا لحالهم وصفتهم.

Vol. 4, p. 206

Q 41:53–54 · Vol. 4, pp. 206–207

Verses 53 to 54

The verses as the commentary quotes them
We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. But is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness? (53) Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably, He is encompassing all things (54)
سَنُرِيهِمْ آياتِنا فِي الْآفاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ (53) أَلا إِنَّهُمْ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْ لِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ أَلا إِنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحِيطٌ (54)
Vol. 4, p. 206
"We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves": he means what God, Mighty and Majestic, made easy for His Messenger ﷺ and for the caliphs after him and the helpers of His religion, in the horizons of the world and the lands of the East and the West generally, and in the courtyard of the Arabs «1»
سَنُرِيهِمْ آياتِنا فِي الْآفاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ يعنى ما يسر الله عز وجل لرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وللخلفاء من بعده ونصار دينه في آفاق الدنيا وبلاد المشرق والمغرب عموما وفي باحة العرب «1»
Vol. 4, p. 207
especially: of conquests the like of which were not made easy for any of the caliphs of the earth before them, and of the triumph over the tyrants and the Chosroes, and the prevailing of their few over their many, and the setting of their weak over their strong, and His bringing about at their hands matters beyond the customary, breaking the habitual patterns; and the spreading of the call of Islam in the regions of the inhabited world, and the extension of its state to its farthest reaches. Induction (al-istiqra') in the histories and the recorded books, on the battlefields of its people and their battle-days, informs you of wonders: you will not see one of their battles but a sign among the signs of God and a verse among His verses, with which certainty is strengthened and faith increased, and it becomes clear that the religion of Islam is the religion of truth, from which none turns away except one who contradicts his own perception and deceives himself; and steadfastness and constancy are only the attribute of truth and sincerity, just as agitation and shaking are the attribute of fabrication and falsehood, and falsehood has a wind that flutters and then subsides, and a dominion that appears and then dissipates. "In your Lord" (bi-rabbika) is in the position of the nominative, as the agent of "kafa" (suffices). And "that He is over all things a Witness" is a substitute for it; its implied construction is: "or is it not sufficient for them that your Lord is, over all things, a Witness?" And its meaning: that this promised [matter], the manifestation of the signs of God in the horizons and within themselves, they will see and behold, and at that point it will become clear to them that the Qur'an is the revelation of the Knower of the unseen, who is over all things a Witness, that is, an overseeing watcher to whom His unseen and His seen are alike; so that suffices them as a proof that it is true and that it is from Him; and had it not been so, this force would not have been strengthened, nor would its bearers have been given this victory. It is also read: "fi mirya," with damm [on the mim], and it is doubt. "Encompassing": knowing the things in their totality and their details, their outward and inward aspects, so that nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He is requiting them for their disbelief and their doubt about the meeting with their Lord. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Whoever recites Surah al-Sajdah, God gives him ten good deeds for every letter" «1».
خصوصا: من الفتوح التي لم يتيسر أمثالها لأحد من خلفاء الأرض قبلهم، ومن الإظهار على الجبابرة والأكاسرة، وتغليب قليلهم على كثيرهم، وتسليط ضعافهم على أقويائهم، وإجرائه على أيديهم أمورا خارجة من المعهود خارقة للعادات، ونشر دعوة الإسلام في أقطار المعمورة، وبسط دولته في أقاصيها، والاستقراء يطلعك في التواريخ والكتب المدوّنة في مشاهد أهله وأيامهم: على عجائب لا ترى وقعة من وقائعهم إلا علما من أعلام الله وآية من آياته، يقوى معها اليقين، ويزداد بها الإيمان، ويتبين أن دين الإسلام هو دين الحق الذي لا يحيد عنه إلا مكابر حسه مغالط نفسه، وما الثبات والاستقامة إلا صفة الحق والصدق، كما أن الاضطراب والتزلزل صفة الفرية والزور، وأن للباطل ريحا تخفق ثم تسكن، ودولة تظهر ثم تضمحل بِرَبِّكَ في موضع الرفع على أنه فاعل كفى. وأَنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ بدل منه، تقديره. أو لم يكفهم أن ربك على كل شيء شهيد. ومعناه: أن هذا الموعود من إظهار آيات الله في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم سيرونه ويشاهدونه، فيتبينون عند ذلك أن القرآن تنزيل عالم الغيب الذي هو على كل شيء شهيد، أى: مطلع مهيمن يستوي عنده غيبه وشهادته، فيكفيهم ذلك دليلا على أنه حق وأنه من عنده، ولو لم يكن كذلك لما قوى هذه القوة ولما نصر حاملوه هذه النصرة. وقرئ: في مرية، بالضم وهي الشك مُحِيطٌ عالم يجمل الأشياء وتفاصيلها وظواهرها وبواطنها، فلا تخفى عليه خافية منهم، وهو مجازيهم على كفرهم ومريتهم في لقاء ربهم. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة السجدة أعطاه الله بكل حرف عشر حسنات» «1» .
